messages.body_plain:
Hi Kiya, Juliana and Jairo,
Part 2 and 4 use all blocks of 24 hours in a measurement (midnight to
midnight or noon to noon respectively), while GGIR part 5 requires
time blocks from waking up in the morning till waking up the next day
and only if the monitor is worn enough during both the day and the
night.
As a result you typically lose most of the first 24 hours because the
measurement often starts after waking up, and because the last night
is also skipped in part 5 you also loose around 24 hours at the end.
This explains why output for part 5 typically has less days.
I looked at this critically when I developed it, but it could still be
worth looking at it again to see whether there is a way to maybe
extract partial information about the first and last days of the
measurement.
Vincent

messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Time Zone
messages.body_plain:
Hi Xueping,
Does this error still persist in the latest version of GGIR?
I see on wikipedia <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_tz_database_time_zones> that  America/New_York is not exactly the same as EST, which is  America/Cancun <https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=America/Cancun&action=edit&redlink=1>. Maybe that explains your error? Timestamps can exist in one timezone but not in the other when clock changes happen in a different hour of the night.
Thanks, Vincent
PS: Please try to post issues on https://github.com/wadpac/GGIR/issues next time, as that makes it easier to handle them.

Hi Juliana,
It is not only the first and last day that are ignored in part5. I designed part5 to only include full windows lasting from waking up to waking up, and to never consider the last day, the before last day after waking up, and the first day of measurement.
I did this because I was not sure whether 'waking up' could reliably be detected on the first and last day, if people only start wearing the accelerometer on the second day when they wake up or and take it off in the last evening then this is true.

Thanks to work by Jairo, we may be able to give you the option to extract results from more days in the next release of GGIR.
Best wishes, Vincent

messages.subject: GGIR version 1.5-21 with improved part 5
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,

GGIR version 1.5-21 is now on CRAN (for Linux and Windows, Mac version should follow soon).

Thanks to contributions from Jairo, part 5 of GGIR is now able to extract output for all measurement days. We have known for a while that part 5 was not optimal, and it is great that this is finally addressed.

Like before, you can use part 5 by giving argument 'mode' in g.shell.GGIR the value 5.

Please note that if you use argument timewindow = "MM" then the output of part 5 represents a day defined from midnight to midnight, this means that any sleep estimates for that day represent parts of sleep from two distinct nights. If you want the part 5 sleep estimates to correspond to a single night then use timewindow = "WW". If you want both to be stored in the output then use: timewindow = c("MM","WW").

The new argument excludefirstlast.part5 allows you to exclude the first and last day of measurement for this analysis (default value = FALSE). The older argument "excludefirstlast" refers to the sleep analysis and influences whether you want to analyse the first and last night for sleep. It is best to leave this set at FALSE (default) if your research focuses on part5.

Note that the argument previously present 'dayborder' also works for part 5, so you can decide where a day ends (e.g. default is midnight, but you may be interested in 3am-3am windows).

In addition to the updates in part 5, Vincent added various checks and tiny improvements to part 4 to catch extreme cases that caused the code to run into errors. Data that may previously may have been hard to process, should hopefully now result in less problems.

Finally. we reduced the size of the example data and the vignette images to reduce the overall package size.

Vincent and Jairo
